ai-at-work.title: Bot-detection startup Spur nabs $200M from Insight
ai-at-work.excerpt: Spur Intelligence has raised a $200 million round from Insight Partners for its tech that can identify legit human traffic from bots.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Spur Intelligence just closed a $200 million funding round with Insight Partners to scale up its bot detection technology. This matters because digital workplaces are increasingly under siege from automated attacks, fraudulent access attempts, and credential stuffing that can compromise security and data integrity. Here's the thing though: throwing $200 million at bot detection is like buying an expensive lock after someone's already jimmied your door open, which means companies still need to focus on solid identity verification and access controls first.

ai-at-work.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
ai-at-work.excerpt: Since launching last year, the startup today has more than 8 million people using the open source or hosted version of its models, and now generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Fish Audio just raised fifty-two million dollars to scale up their AI voice generation tools, which already have eight million users and are pulling in twenty-one million in annual recurring revenue. This matters because voice cloning and synthetic speech are coming to your digital workplace whether you're ready or not, from accessibility features to automated content creation to potentially some sketchy deepfake situations you'll need policies for. Look, we've been saying AI audio would be huge for three years, and now it's finally here with real traction, so if your organization hasn't thought about voice AI governance, you're already behind.

ai-at-work.title: Meta to build $14B El Paso data center campus with BlackRock

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Meta and BlackRock are dropping $14 billion on a new AI data center campus in El Paso, Texas, marking a serious bet on infrastructure for training and running large language models. This matters because your workplace collaboration tools, search functions, and generative AI features all depend on massive compute resources, and when giants like Meta invest this heavily in infrastructure, it signals where the market's going and what capabilities will actually be available to enterprises. Here's the thing though: everyone's building data centers like they're going out of style, which means the real differentiator won't be compute capacity for much longer, it'll be what you actually do with it.

ai-at-work.title: AI researchers call for new tools that can slow automated model development
ai-at-work.excerpt: A group of tech workers today published an open letter that calls for a new approach to regulating automated artificial intelligence development initiatives. All the document’s 1,134 signatories work
ai-at-work.dwp_take: AI researchers from major companies like OpenAI, Google, and Meta signed an open letter asking for new regulatory tools to slow down automated AI model development. This matters to digital workplace pros because uncontrolled AI development directly impacts the tools, policies, and skills we'll need to manage in our organizations going forward. Here's the thing: when the people building these systems are the ones asking for the brakes, maybe pay attention, because they're basically saying "we're moving too fast even for us."

tools-tech.title: How to remap the Copilot key on your keyboard to something more helpful
tools-tech.excerpt: Pressing the Copilot key on your laptop keyboard launches Copilot. But whether or not you use Microsoft's AI, you can remap the key to trigger a different feature.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft stuck a dedicated Copilot key on millions of keyboards, and now people are scrambling to turn it into something actually useful. This matters because it's a perfect example of feature bloat meeting real user needs, and shows how vendors still don't get that not everyone wants their pet technology shoved into the hardware. Look, I've been doing this for three decades, and the Copilot key is basically the digital equivalent of a car manufacturer gluing a cup holder to your steering wheel.

tools-tech.title: Token-maxing is an AI cost sink - how to use agents without busting your budget
tools-tech.excerpt: Professionals are burning through tokens, but smart business leaders are finding ways to balance costs and value creation.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Companies are discovering that their AI agent implementations are hemorrhaging money through excessive token consumption, which happens when systems process way more data than necessary to complete tasks. For digital workplace leaders rolling out AI assistants and automation, this is the difference between a smart investment and accidentally funding someone's AI hobby project. The real trick isn't buying the fanciest agent on the market, it's teaching your organization to ask smarter questions so the AI doesn't have to read your entire email archive just to schedule a meeting.

tools-tech.title: AI has become Apple’s latest bug detective
tools-tech.excerpt: Artificial intelligence is becoming a force multiplier for Apple security research. Apple’s latest 26.5.2 software update includes patches for a record number of bugs — many of them identified by secu
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple used AI tools to identify and fix a record 242 security vulnerabilities across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS in a single update cycle. This matters because it shows how AI is becoming table stakes for catching security gaps that traditional manual review misses, and your organization's security posture depends on keeping pace with this reality. The irony is that we've spent years warning people about AI risks while the real story is AI quietly becoming the only practical way to handle the sheer volume of vulnerabilities modern systems generate.

tools-tech.title: Synsira Launches Kind Local Pro with 100% On-Device AI
tools-tech.excerpt: Operating entirely offline, Kind Local Pro gives individuals local data sovereignty without sacrificing AI performance Synsira Software is addressing the biggest concern with AI: privacy. Today, the c
tools-tech.dwp_take: Synsira just released Kind Local Pro, an AI tool that runs entirely on your own computer without sending anything to the cloud. For digital workplace folks, this matters because it finally addresses the privacy nightmare that's been keeping security teams up at night while IT tries to figure out what employees are actually doing with ChatGPT. Honestly, after years of watching companies panic about data leaving the building, it's refreshing to see someone build something that lets people use AI without playing roulette with their sensitive information.

digital-culture.title: Warren Buffett is often asked what the ideal workplace is. His answer is the best career tip you’ll hear today
digital-culture.excerpt: For Warren Buffett’s authorized biography, The Snowball: Warren Buffett and the Business of Life, the billionaire investor gave writer Alice Schroeder unprecedented access to explore his opinions and
digital-culture.dwp_take: Warren Buffett told biographer Alice Schroeder that people should work somewhere they genuinely want to be, not just chase prestige or money. This matters because digital workplace leaders spend millions on retention and engagement programs when the real answer might just be hiring people who actually want to show up. Here's the kicker: if your workplace needs that much convincing to keep people around, you've probably already lost the game.

digital-culture.title: Would you work harder if you knew your boss was anti-union?
digital-culture.excerpt: Unions have grown more popular in recent years, with 16.5 million workers represented by a union in 2025—the highest share of the overall workforce in 16 years. As workers have mounted high-profile un
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new study is examining whether workers actually change their behavior and effort levels when they know their employer actively opposes unionization. This matters to digital workplace leaders because it touches on a fundamental question of trust and engagement: if your workforce knows you're against their organizing, does that kill morale and productivity, or does transparency actually help? After 30 years in this space, I can tell you that pretending you have no position on unions while your employees whisper about it anyway is the worst possible strategy—just pick a lane and own it.

digital-culture.title: You have a big idea. Here’s how to turn it into impact
digital-culture.excerpt: Peter Drucker was the quintessential management visionary. Often decades ahead of his time, he developed concepts like the knowledge worker and management by objectives long before they were on anybod
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is dusting off Peter Drucker's playbook to remind us that turning ideas into actual impact requires more than just having a good thought at 2am. This matters because digital workplace folks spend half their time pitching initiatives that go nowhere, and the other half wondering why leadership doesn't listen. The irony is that Drucker figured this out decades ago, which means we've been ignoring the same lessons for thirty years and calling it innovation.

digital-culture.title: AI may finally make ‘women’s work’ valuable. But will women benefit?
digital-culture.excerpt: For years, economists have predicted that artificial intelligence would hollow out the labor market. Machines would write the code, analyze the contracts, draft the emails, and automate the work that
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is reporting that AI could ironically elevate traditionally undervalued "women's work" like caregiving and mentoring by automating the technical tasks that currently dominate workplace hierarchies. This matters to digital workplace pros because it forces us to confront whether our tools and platforms actually reward relationship-based skills or if we're just automating our way to the same old gender pay gap with fancier technology. Spoiler alert: AI doesn't fix culture, and until organizations actually pay people for soft skills the way they pay engineers, this is just another way to say women's work will still be undervalued, just in a more efficient economy.

industry-news.title: Amazon Reportedly Plans to Consolidate Nova AI Models
industry-news.excerpt: Amazon reportedly plans to consolidate several Nova AI models. Here’s what the strategy shift could mean for AWS and enterprise AI customers. The post Amazon Reportedly Plans to Consolidate Nova AI Mo
industry-news.dwp_take: Amazon is reportedly consolidating its Nova AI model lineup instead of maintaining multiple versions across different capabilities. This matters because enterprises evaluating AWS for their AI strategy need to understand which models will stick around and which ones might get the axe, affecting long-term platform decisions. Consolidation usually sounds like efficiency speak, but it's really Amazon saying "we built too many things" and hoping you don't notice the feature set you were counting on disappeared.

industry-news.title: More Than 45,000 Software Flaws Reported as AI Reshapes Cybersecurity
industry-news.excerpt: AI security tools are helping uncover more software flaws, creating new patching demands and potential offensive risks for enterprise IT teams. The post More Than 45,000 Software Flaws Reported as AI
industry-news.dwp_take: AI security tools are finding software flaws faster than we can patch them, with over 45,000 vulnerabilities now on the radar. For digital workplace teams, this means your IT security folks are drowning in a fire hose of work that'll keep them busy for years. The irony here is we asked AI to help us find problems and it said "hold my beer" and found so many problems that we're now the bottleneck instead of the tools.

industry-news.excerpt: G Suite Basic, Business, and Enterprise users can now check grammar in Google Docs. Here's a quick look at how well the feature performs compared to alternatives. The post 5 Google Docs Grammar Check

industry-news.title: Apple Fixes 194 Security Flaws Across iPhone, Mac and Other Devices
industry-news.excerpt: Apple’s latest iPhone, iPad and Mac updates patch 194 unique security flaws involving root access, kernel code execution and protected data. The post Apple Fixes 194 Security Flaws Across iPhone, Mac
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple released security patches addressing 194 vulnerabilities across iPhones, iPads, and Macs, with several flaws allowing kernel-level access and data theft. Digital workplace pros need to prioritize these updates immediately since most organizations now run Apple devices and a single unpatched machine can compromise your entire network. Here's the thing: 194 sounds dramatic until you realize it's basically Apple saying "oops, we left the doors unlocked" multiple times over.
